Springsteen on Broadway, meanwhile, occupies a category of its own — a solo performance piece that critics describe as emotionally raw and deliberately stripped of the spectacle audiences might expect from a stadium-scale artist. With over forty critical assessments contributing to its score, it represents one of the more broadly evaluated productions on the list.

Across the top-rated shows, the average critic score holds at 88 out of 100, reflecting a genuinely strong season rather than a handful of outliers inflating the rankings. Productions range from one-woman showcases to long-running visual spectacles, offering entry points for a wide range of theatergoing preferences. Those planning a visit to New York this month would do well to check current availability, as run lengths and scheduling vary considerably.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
As Broadway's fall season reaches its peak in November 2026, the city's stages are offering some of the most critically celebrated productions in recent memory. The shows that opened in 2022 continue to draw audiences and earn exceptional marks from critics, with an average score hovering around 90 out of 100 — a remarkably high bar across the board.

At the top of the rankings, Jamie Lloyd's radical reimagining of Cyrano De Bergerac leads with a 94/100, with critics consistently praising its daring, modern-dress approach to Rostand's classic. Close behind, the revival of Jez Butterworth's Jerusalem earns a 93/100, driven in large part by what many reviewers are calling a career-defining performance from Mark Rylance — a towering piece of work that has cemented the production's reputation as a modern theatrical landmark.

Among musicals, Into the Woods and Kimberly Akimbo stand out as particular highlights. The Sondheim revival earns praise for its pared-down, near-perfect staging, while Kimberly Akimbo has won over critics with its rare ability to balance sharp comedy with genuine emotional depth.

What is perhaps most striking about the current landscape is its range. The top-rated shows span intimate one-man performances, sweeping ensemble dramas, and reimagined classics, reflecting a Broadway season that rewards both ambition and craft. Jack Holden's solo show Cruise, addressing the AIDS crisis in 1980s Soho, and the revival of Andrea Levy's Small Island both demonstrate that serious, socially resonant storytelling remains very much at the heart of what critics are responding to this season.

For theatergoers looking to make the most of what remains of the fall season, the highest-rated productions listed here offer a strong and reliable starting point.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
As November 2026 arrives, Broadway's 2023 season continues to demonstrate remarkable staying power, with the top-rated shows maintaining critical scores that cluster impressively around 89 out of 100 — a testament to the caliber of work that defined that year's theatrical landscape.

Leading the rankings is Crazy for You, the Gershwin revival that critics have consistently described as musical theatre heaven, driven in large part by Susan Stroman's choreography. Close behind, Operation Mincemeat stands as one of the more surprising success stories of the era — a homegrown WWII musical that critics praised for its tonal range and inventive staging, and which has accumulated the broadest critical consensus of any production in this group. Groundhog Day, adapted from the beloved film, rounds out the upper tier, with Tim Minchin's score and Matthew Warchus's direction earning it the designation of "instant classic" from multiple reviewers.

Beyond the frontrunners, the list reflects a season of notable range. Pearl Cleage's Blues for an Alabama Sky and For Black Boys Who Have Considered Suicide When the Hue Gets Too Heavy both earned strong marks for productions that centered underrepresented stories with craft and emotional depth. Dear England, James Graham's drama examining Gareth Southgate's tenure leading the England football team, demonstrates how sports and national identity can serve as compelling theatrical subject matter.

Critic scores here draw from verified professional reviews, and the rankings reflect aggregate assessments rather than any single perspective. For theatergoers looking to engage with the defining productions of 2023, the highest-rated shows in this guide offer a reliable starting point — and checking current availability remains the essential next step before planning a visit.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
As Broadway moves through the fall of 2026, the top-rated shows currently running include several productions that opened in 2024 and have sustained remarkable critical momentum. The average critic score across the highest-rated offerings sits at 90 out of 100, reflecting an unusually strong season by any measure.

Among the standouts, War Horse leads the rankings with a near-perfect 96 from critics, who continue to describe its life-sized horse puppetry as a genuinely rare theatrical achievement. The production represents the kind of large-scale physical storytelling that remains difficult to replicate, and its critical consensus has held firm across multiple reviews. Stereophonic, David Adjmi's immersive drama set inside a 1970s recording studio, has drawn the broadest critical attention of any show on the list, accumulating 31 reviews while maintaining an 88 score — a signal of both its reach and its staying power. Critics have called it one of the most significant American plays in recent memory. People, Places and Things also warrants attention, with 24 reviews and an 89 score anchored by what critics consistently describe as a career-defining central performance.

Beyond these titles, the list reflects considerable range. The Lehman Trilogy brings its epic, three-hour scope back to audiences for a third run. Gatz offers an eight-hour word-for-word adaptation of The Great Gatsby for theatergoers willing to commit to something genuinely unconventional. For Black Boys Who Have Considered Suicide When the Hue Gets Too Heavy continues to draw strong notices for its emotional depth and cultural urgency.

For anyone planning a visit to Broadway this November, consulting the full rankings and reading individual critic summaries is the most reliable way to match a production to your own interests and availability.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
As November 2026 arrives, Broadway's 2025 season stands as a remarkable chapter in the art form's history, with the top-rated shows earning an average critic score of 90 out of 100 — a testament to the extraordinary level of work currently on offer.

Leading the field is Mark Rosenblatt's Giant, which carries its Olivier Award momentum to New York with a near-universal critical reception and a score of 94. Reviewers describe it as bold and urgent, signaling that this exploration of Roald Dahl's legacy has lost none of its force in translation. Close behind, the revival of The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee has drawn some of the season's most enthusiastic notices, with critics calling it joyous and sparkling — a production that reminds audiences what musical comedy, at its best, can accomplish.

Among the season's more distinctive offerings, Teatro La Plaza's Spanish-language Hamlet — performed by eight actors with Down syndrome — has earned serious critical attention, with reviewers noting its power and depth rather than treating it as a novelty. It reflects a broader pattern in this season's highest-rated work: productions that take genuine creative and social risks tend to be the ones critics return to most urgently.

The range on display this season is considerable, spanning Greek epic, Orwellian allegory, WWII biography, and Tony Kushner's Angels in America, each finding fresh theatrical language for its source material. Whether audiences are seeking an emotionally demanding evening or something more celebratory, the current crop of top-rated productions offers substantive choices across genres and styles.

Tickets for several of these productions are in high demand, and theatergoers are encouraged to check availability and book ahead to secure their preferred dates before the holiday season accelerates.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
Broadway's fall 2026 season has delivered a range of productions spanning intimate docudrama, sharp comedy, and crowd-pleasing spectacle, with the top-rated shows averaging a strong 77 out of 100 among critics.

Leading the pack is Downstate, Bruce Norris's unflinching examination of life after incarceration, which critics are calling a must-see Broadway triumph. With 18 reviews in and an 88 critic score, it stands as the season's most acclaimed work—provocative and gut-wrenching in equal measure. Close behind it, School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play earns an 84, with reviewers consistently highlighting Jocelyn Bioh's sharp comic writing and Whitney White's exuberant direction as a winning combination that manages to be both funny and genuinely insightful.

Among the season's more unexpected entries, Billy Crystal 860 has resonated deeply with audiences and critics alike. Crystal's one-man show, which draws directly from his experience losing his home in the 2025 Palisades Fire, earns an 82 and has been praised for its rare balance of grief and humor. Here There Are Blueberries, a Holocaust docudrama from Moisés Kaufman and the Tectonic Theater Project, also draws strong notices at 81, with critics calling it essential and powerful theater.

Not every production has found consensus. Other Desert Cities benefits from a starry cast that includes Julia Louis-Dreyfus making her Broadway debut alongside Ed Harris and Lily Rabe, though critics find the production itself somewhat uneven. A Few Good Men sits at the lower end of the rankings despite admirable staging from director Michael Arden.

With the holiday season approaching, now is a practical time to secure tickets, as the top-rated shows are likely to see increased demand through December.

best-new-broadway-shows.intro:
November 2026 brings a notably strong season to Broadway, with the top-rated shows averaging well above the norm and several productions generating genuine critical conversation. Whether you're drawn to challenging drama, sharp comedy, or intimate solo performance, this month's offerings reflect a wide range of theatrical ambition.

Leading the pack is Downstate, Bruce Norris's provocative drama receiving widespread critical acclaim for its unflinching examination of difficult moral terrain. Directed with precision and purpose, it stands as one of the more talked-about Broadway productions in recent memory. Close behind is School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play, Jocelyn Bioh's sharp-edged comedy earning praise for both its wit and its substance, elevated further by Whitney White's energetic direction and a committed ensemble cast.

Elsewhere on the list, Here There Are Blueberries offers a haunting docudrama approach to Holocaust history that many critics are calling essential viewing, while Other Desert Cities brings a starry cast — including Julia Louis-Dreyfus in her Broadway debut — to Jon Robin Baitz's family drama, though critical response there has been more measured.

Not every production this month has landed with equal force, and scores across the list reflect real variation in critical opinion. As reviews continue to accumulate and word of mouth develops throughout the month, the rankings below offer a useful starting point for deciding where to spend your time and money on Broadway this November.

broadway-shows-closing-soon.intro:
As Broadway heads into the final weeks of 2026, a compelling mix of dramatic theater and crowd-pleasing musicals is preparing to close, making now the time to catch these productions before they exit the stage for good.

Leading the pack is Downstate, which stands as the highest-rated show on this list with an 88 out of 100 from critics. Bruce Norris's unflinching drama has earned widespread acclaim for its provocative storytelling and masterful direction, and it represents the kind of challenging, essential theater that rarely comes along. Close behind is SIX, the pop-concert musical reimagining the lives of Henry VIII's six wives, which continues to earn praise for its energy, vocal performances, and crowd-pleasing appeal. For audiences drawn to more somber material, Here There Are Blueberries offers a haunting and critically lauded docudrama that critics have called essential viewing, earning an 81 out of 100 across 25 reviews.

Beyond the top-rated shows, the closing list reflects Broadway's characteristic range. Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York) brings a charming, small-scale intimacy to the stage, while the effects-driven spectacle of Stranger Things: The First Shadow caters to audiences seeking a more immersive theatrical experience. The average critic score across these productions sits at 66 out of 100, suggesting a season with genuine standouts alongside more divisive offerings.

With closing dates approaching, ticket availability for the most acclaimed productions is likely to become increasingly limited. Audiences who have been waiting for the right moment to see any of these shows would do well to check current schedules and secure seats sooner rather than later.
